agent.problem: This non-opening story card has four sentences: the statement about purification, "Not everything.", "NEARLY everything.", and the closing joke. Non-opening story cards are limited to two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: "fewer" is not unambiguously wrong. Although verse 23 says "better," verses 25-26 contrast repeated offerings with Christ's single offering, so a baker could argue that the heavenly things were purified with fewer sacrifices.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

human.problem: Papa Dorin links Christ's second appearing (Hebrews 9:28) to his own mission with 'THAT is why these ovens stay warm.' This implies the second appearing is tied to the Marriage Supper of the Lamb, which Hebrews 9 doesn't mention. It also has no Matthew 24:36 reference, which papa-dorin.md points to when the Supper's timing comes up.
human.question: When a passage speaks of Christ's return, may Papa Dorin tie it to his mission and the Marriage Supper as his own in-world reaction? Or does that count as connecting passages beyond what the text states? If it is allowed, must he also cite Matthew 24:36 or Revelation 19?
